plan.goal: Size the PLINK binary .bed dataset and per-chromosome files for a GWAS genotype cohort of 17785 samples and 7476277 variants (260245 on the largest chromosome).
plan.rationale: The binary .bed format packs 2 bits per sample per variant (4 samples/byte), so the whole-dataset .bed size is n_samples × n_variants / 4 / 1e6 MB. The per-chromosome .bed applies the same 2-bits rule to a single chromosome's variant count. With ~7.5M variants and 260K on the largest chromosome, this is a dense human imputed GWAS, so the standard 25 per-chromosome files (chr1-22, X, Y, MT) apply. The largest chromosome (chr1) carries 260245 variants.
caveats: Per-chromosome file count assumes the standard human chromosome set (chr1-22, X, Y, MT = 25 files); confirm the dataset omits or includes sex/mitochondrial chromosomes.
The chr1 per-chromosome .bed (~1.16 GB) is the largest; smaller chromosomes are proportionally smaller.
Budget disk for the full ~33 GB .bed plus the .bim/.fam/.bed trio and downstream PLINK output, which can be several-fold larger.
